title: Stage enumeration invariant
statement: Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a counting state. For $u,v\in\mathbb N$, write $R(u,v)$ for the assertion that the oracle returns true on the type-$3$ query encoding $(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$; write $I(u)$ for the assertion that it returns true on the type-$1$ query encoding $(x,u,\sigma.s)$; and let $\operatorname{Ball}_j$ be the set of numbers below $\sigma.K$ reachable from some $I$-witness by at most $j$ steps of $R$. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.i\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.i1=\sigma.i+1$, $\sigma.cp=|\operatorname{Ball}_{\sigma.i}|$, and $\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=\sigma.u=\sigma.cnt=0$. If, for all $v',c'\le B$, the comparison-stage machine initialized with $i=K$, $i1=K+1$, $v=v'$, $c=c'$, and $cp=|\operatorname{Ball}_K|$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the stage-head machine initialized in state $\sigma$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds and no member of $\operatorname{Ball}_j$ is accepted by the type-$2$ oracle query for any $j$ with $\sigma.i<j\le\sigma.K$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal O$ is an oracle on four query types and binary words
Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
$\sigma.cp$ equals the cardinality of the ball at stage $\sigma.i$
For every $v',c'\le B$, the specified comparison-stage computation satisfies $Q$ exactly and terminates within register bound $B$
caveat: The formal statement uses the definitions of the balls and machine semantics; the prose spells out the oracle queries and consequence.

Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle,
let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a register state with every register at
most $B$. Write $R(u,v)$ for the assertion that the oracle's type-$3$ query on
$(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$ is true, and $I(u)$ for the assertion that its type-$1$ query on
$(x,u,\sigma.s)$ is true; let $\operatorname{Ball}_j$ be the set of codes below
$\sigma.K$ that are reachable from some $I$-code by at most $j$ steps of $R$. Suppose
$\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.i\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.i1=\sigma.i+1$,
$\sigma.cp=|\operatorname{Ball}_{\sigma.i}|$, and
$\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=\sigma.u=\sigma.cnt=0$. If, for every $v',c'\le B$, the
machine initialized at the comparison stage with $i=K$, $i1=K+1$, outer registers
$v',c'$, and $cp=|\operatorname{Ball}_K|$ terminates within register bound $B$ and
accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the machine initialized at the stage head with
state $\sigma$ terminates within that bound and accepts exactly when both $Q$ holds and
no code in $\operatorname{Ball}_j$ is accepted by the oracle for any
$\sigma.i<j\le\sigma.K$.
